key_insight: The paper reports sharper knot-ropelength lower bounds: L ≥ 2.0996C^(3/4) for crossing number C and L ≥ π(s−1) for stick number s.
engineering_relevance: These bounds provide theoretical benchmarks for optimizing knotted filaments and assessing geometric packing constraints.
method: Use LLM assistance to develop mathematical bounds.
Separate local and global terms in an optimization integral.
Relate ropelength to stick number and optimize a standard torus-knot parameterization.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improving the universal coefficient from 1.105 to 2.0996 and obtaining stronger lower bounds for at least 41 torus knots and a specific pretzel-knot class.
watch_item: LLM assistance did not yield improvements to the coefficients or scaling of known universal upper bounds.
paper_title: LLM-Assisted Advances in the Ropelength Problem
